recipes.name: Country Apple Dumplings
ingredients_raw: 2 large Granny Smith apples, peeled and cored
2 (10 ounce) cans refrigerated crescent roll dough
1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle Mountain Dew ™

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Cut each apple into 8 equal wedges; set aside.

Separate crescent roll dough into triangles. Roll each apple wedge in a crescent roll triangle, starting at the wide end and rolling toward the pointed tip. Pinch to seal and place in the prepared baking dish.
Melt butter in a small saucepan over low heat. Stir sugar and cinnamon into melted butter until combined. Pour over apple dumplings, followed by soda.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, 35 to 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Country Apple Dumplings
raw_recipe.description: These apple dumplings are made with fresh apples and crescent roll dough, baked with butter, cinnamon sugar, and soda for a fabulous fall treat.

video.description: In this video, Nicole shows you how to make buttery country apple dumplings with a surprising secret ingredient. Using crescent dough rolled apple slices, cover the individual dumplings with homemade buttery cinnamon sauce. With the help of one particular brand of sweet soda, drench the baking dish of dumplings with the drink’s distinct flavor. After baking the apple dumplings in the oven until bubbly, let them cool. They’re delicious, easy, and the ideal Fall snack!

review.reviewBody: My son-in-law is diabetic, so I reduced the butter to 3/4 stick of butter melted with 1/2 cup of Splenda sugar blend, and used Diet Mountain Dew. Wonderful!
I made this tonight they are incredible. I halved the recipe and made one change. I used 3/4 cup sugar(1/2 cup white, 1/4 cup brown). Will be making this again and again.

This is great! Since this is super fattening, I made some changes & couldn't tell any difference. I used reduced fat crescent rolls, cut the sugar to 1/2c. & 1/2 c. splenda & used diet mountain dew. I cut back the butter to 1 stick + 2 tblsp. Does anyone know what the fat grams & calories would be with these changes?

I found this recipe last year and made it for Thanksgiving dinner with my husband's family. Everyone raved about it and made me promise to make it at Christmas. I now make it for a quick and easy dessert for any occasion. Everyone asks for the recipe. I made a few changes to mine though. I use 3-4 large Granny Smith apples, and quarter them. This makes bigger dumplings and each person gets more of the tart apple taste. Before I put the sugar/cinnamon/butter mixture or the Mt. Dew on, I bake the dumplings for 10-12 minutes to avoid having soggy dough. Then, I pour or spoon the sugar mixture over the top and pour just 10 oz. of Mt. Dew around the dumplings, not over the top, and bake for another 25-28 minutes, or until done. They come out firm, not soggy, and wonderfully crunchy on top from the sugar. People can't stop eating them!

This is a very good and easy recipe. The last time I made recipe. I got four large peaches. I peeled and cut each in 1/4. Rolled each 1/4 in one crescent roll triangle. I did cut sugar some. My husband said he liked them better than apple.

I made these several times over the fall. Everyone raved about them. The only addition was a little bit of cardamom and nutmeg sprinkled onto each pastry triangle prior to wrapping it up with the apple, and I do add a tsp of vanilla to the topping after I take it off of the stove. I do pour the soda (used 7 up) into the pan at the side and not over the top of the dough and do this last. I've made it with 8 oz of soda instead of the 12 for a less soupy mixture if there are leftovers. They bake the same but the mixture is thicker. Super easy recipe that is great for a potluck, or quick dessert to go with a nice fall dinner. This is a keeper for me.

I made this recipe twice. First time I follow the recipe precisely. Second time I did some adjustments Reccomended by previous reviewers. Kudos to all of you who made improvements. I have to say for the recipe itself I would give 4-5 stars. For the glorified version of the recipe - 5+ stars and I wish I could give 10 starts!
My adjustments with ingredients: 
1. Butter - only 1.5 sticks
2. Cinnamon - 1.5 teaspoon
3. Sugar - 0.5 cup white + 0.5 cup brown
4. Added 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg (can add more)
5. Added 1 tsp vanilla (can add more)
6. Added 1 Tbsp raw honey (can add more)
7. Added 1 Tbsp rum (can add more, & I think the darker rum the better)
8. Double amount of green apples medium size & cut them in quarters
9. Reduce lemon soda to 10 oz

Adjustments with the process.
Grease the baking pan with about 1/4 of butter stick. Prepare the caramel syrup: melt all sugar, but do not burn. It has to be golden, add butter, then cinnamon, nutmeg. The last - honey, vanilla, rum. Keep steering for another 1-2 mins. 
Wrap courters of apples with crescent rolls, arrange on the pan. Bake on its own for 10 mins. take out of the oven, pour carefully with spoon the caramel syrup. Put back in the oven for another 10 mins. Then pour lime or other sour soda (I had ginger ale) around the dumplings, but NOT OVER it. Bake for another 25 mins. It turned out like a gourmet dessert. Was a huge hit at a party.

This was an easy delicious recipe. I used red delicious apples because we had lots of them and I needed to use them up. I also used 3/4 cup of Pyure organic Stevia...I should have used 1/2 cup since the apples were already sweet and I’m not really fond of very sweet desserts. Also I cooked it in my Oster countertop oven at 325 for 25 minutes because I also baked them on turbo. They were perfect! Will definitely make them again using the Granny Smith apples.

1. Made a little white sugar/cinnamon/pinch of nutmeg mixture. Ran apple pieces in a colander under water to moisten them so the spices would stick, rolled apple in mixture. 2. Added 1/8 tsp nutmeg to mixture I boiled (1/2c white sugar, 1/4 brown sugar, 1 cup). Boiled until thick and all the sugar was melted. Added a little bit of vanilla extract before I poured over the dumplings. At the end the dumpling had puffed up and were floating on the liquids, nice and pretty crisp.
I used 1 cup sugar and 1/2C brown sugar with 2 teaspoons of cinnamon I've made them both ways I love them both. Thank you for this recipe

My husband loved these. The only thing I would do different is to reduce the butter mixture by half and only use half the amount of soda. I followed the instructions and they were very soggy and did not cook very well on the bottom.

These were absolutely delicious! I made these with only a couple small tweaks. I only had macintosh apples on hand so that's what I used. I mixed 1 tsp cinnamon, 1/4c white sugar & 1/8 tsp nutmeg and rolled the apple wedges in it before covering with the dough. I placed all 16 crescent rolls touching in a 9x13 pan. For the sauce I used 1 cup white sugar & 1/2 cup brown sugar and added 1/4 tsp nutmeg. Everything else I kept the same. Mine were done at exactly 40 mins. They puffed up beautifully and were a dark golden brown. The sauce was very thick when they finished. The bottoms were also cooked and not doughy. Served each with a little sauce from the pan poured over top. We loved these. I will be making them again.

I use puff pastry and a pizza cutter to cut into triangles. I also sprinkle each apple with brown sugar, cinnamon and nutmeg before rolling in the pastry. I use half brown sugar and white sugar for the sauce along with more cinnamon and nutmeg and use water instead of soda. I bring it to a boil and simmer for a few minutes to thicken before pouring over dumplings.
No changes
Easy to make and so delicious!!!! A keeper for sure.

I'm not much on baking, but I do love pastries and sweet desserts. I made this, it was so easy and WOW! It didn't last two days, my whole family loved it. Thank you for making it soooo easy...trying peach cobbler next!
I’ve made this for 15 ish years, but with OJ and a little zest. Looks like it cooks up the same otherwise. It’s a great quick delish dessert, I love fruity baked treats.
Looks Delicious
This recipe is simple to follow and the results are delicious
Delicious and simple. Served with vanilla ice cream and caramel sauce and it was amazing!
